source.title: The Base64 Data Encodings: base64 and base64url

requirements.quote: Implementations MUST NOT add line feeds to base-encoded data unless the specification referring to this document explicitly directs base encoders to add line feeds after a specific number of characters.
Implementations MUST include appropriate pad characters at the end of encoded data unless the specification referring to this document explicitly states otherwise.

Implementations MUST reject the encoded data if it contains characters outside the base alphabet when interpreting base-encoded data, unless the specification referring to this document explicitly states otherwise.
These pad bits MUST be set to zero by conforming encoders, which is described in the descriptions on padding below.
In some environments, the alteration is critical and therefore decoders MAY chose to reject an encoding if the pad bits have not been set to zero.
The encoding process represents 24-bit groups of input bits as output strings of 4 encoded characters.
Each 6-bit group is used as an index into an array of 64 printable characters.
Padding at the end of the data is performed using the '=' character.

clauses.title: the standard encoding of n bytes is 4 * ceil(n / 3) characters
the URL encoding of n bytes is ceil(4 * n / 3) characters, with no padding
the standard encoding ends in as many "=" as the final group is short of three bytes
base64EncodedLength(n) is the length of the standard encoding of n bytes
a character outside the standard alphabet, whitespace included, anywhere, is refused
a byte at or above 0x80, anywhere in the text, is refused by base64StdPadDecodedLength
a character outside the URL alphabet, "+", "/", "=" and whitespace included, anywhere, is refused
a standard text whose last character carries nonzero pad bits is refused: every text decoded re-encodes to itself
a URL text whose last character carries nonzero pad bits is refused: every text decoded re-encodes to itself
the standard decoding of the standard encoding of b is b
base64StdPadDecodedLength of the standard encoding of b is the length of b
base64StdPadEncodeInto writes the bytes of the standard encoding
base64EncodeInto writes the bytes of the standard encoding
a standard text whose length is not a multiple of four is refused
a standard text with "=" anywhere but its last two characters, or "=" before a non-pad character, is refused
a standard text ending in "===" is refused
the URL encoding is the standard one with "+" and "/" as "-" and "_" and the padding dropped
the URL decoding of the URL encoding of b is b
a URL text of length 1 modulo 4 is refused
a URL text with "=" anywhere, padding included, is refused
